short: An Allied amphibious landing on the Italian coast intended to bypass the Winter Line and capture Rome, which degenerated into a grueling stalemate.
full:
On 22 January 1944, Allied forces landed at Anzio and Nettuno behind the German defensive lines in central Italy. Achieving total surprise, the initial landings faced almost no opposition. However, the Allied commander chose to consolidate his beachhead rather than advance immediately on Rome. This hesitation allowed the German army to rush reinforcements to the area and completely surround the beachhead.

For months, the Allied forces were pinned down in a confined area under constant artillery fire and severe counterattacks. The stalemate was only broken in May when a broader Allied offensive shattered the Winter Line to the south, linking up with the breakout from Anzio. The operation successfully tied down significant German resources but failed to rapidly capture Rome or destroy the retreating German Tenth Army.
